findings.description: When the value is one git can't read as a boolean (e.g. `maybe`), the refusal still says "extensions.worktreeConfig is on". The hint then tells the operator to run `git sparse-checkout disable` before the `-C /` unset, but git refuses to open the repo with that value, so `disable` fails. Saying "is on, or holds a value git cannot read" in the problem text, or putting the unset first for that case, would match decision 101's wording.

The WorktreeConfigError hint puts the repo path unquoted into a command the operator is asked to paste (`git -C / config --file ${sanitizeReason(...)} --unset ...`); sanitizeReason does not shell-quote, so a path with a space, `;`, `$(` or a backtick splits or runs on paste. The path is the operator's own registered repo, so this is not session-reachable, but merge-gate.service.ts:745 already wraps paste-ready repo paths in shellWord(); do the same here.

The new sentence in `launchTask`'s comment ("Per-worktree config is refused here too: the launch's own check would refuse it only once the worktree and the row exist, and they then block a retry") restates `assertNoWorktreeConfig`'s JSDoc; general.md §Comments' seam-duplication test and AGENTS.md §Comments say to delete the call-site copy.

`worktreeConfigOn(gitPath, commonDir, env?)`: `verifiedWorktreeGitEnv` passes `env.GIT_COMMON_DIR` and `env` together, so the two can disagree with no stated winner, and `gitPath` is really `runGit`'s cwd (repo path in one caller, worktree path in the other); rename it `cwd`, or drop it since `--file` makes the cwd irrelevant.

`assertNoWorktreeConfig` and `verifiedWorktreeGitEnv` open-code the same `lstatSync(join(<dir>, 'config.worktree')) || worktreeConfigOn(...)` test, differing only in base dir and error class; if the check grows (another config file), both copies need the same edit.

The new decision 101 sentences were spliced into wrapped paragraphs without reflowing: the line ending "...The in-window check refused such a repo only after `startSession` had" and the one ending "...A swap after the check, by a `head` on" run well past the file's ~100-column wrap, and "(security review, 2026-10-23). The in-window check stays as" is left short; reflow both paragraphs.

"git turns it on in the shared config, and `sparse-checkout disable` leaves it on, with `.git/config.worktree` (Apple Git 2.39.5)" is ambiguous about whether git writes the file or disable leaves it behind; say that `disable` leaves both the extension and `.git/config.worktree` in place, as observed on Apple Git 2.39.5.
